questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not only is University of Berkeley a well-known university, it is also located near San Fransisco. I always wanted to experience living in the US and experience their culture. Further more the Bay Area is a hot-spot for innovation within the field of Biotechnology which is what I study at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that is easy to be honest. I have felt quite alone in the whole process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None? but there was a introduction week on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fine to find the place that I lived, but it was very overpriced.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Airbnb is a cheap option. I recommend the cooperative (even though it can be a little bit dirty).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is quite expensive :(....

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult. It was more the application for the student VISA that was quite a tedious process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online platforms.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was more difficult than I am used to but I am very satisfied in the courses I ended up with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the other KU-students! They are just as confused as you are so don't feel embarrassed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took some Phd/MA leveled courses that were very interesting! I could follow the courses but it was a lot of work. The BA chemistry course was quite challenging though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference is that there are exams throughout the semester, instead of one big one at the end of the semester. I found it quite stressfull that almost every week I had some kind of exam or presentation that counted towards my final grade... but you get used to it haha.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cell Engineering 
Inorganic Chemistry in Living Systems
Synthetic Biology 
Basic Principles of Drug Delivery

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend BIOE148 and BIOE124. Fantastic Professors and exciting course material.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the Berkeley Cheese Club! Good vibes and opportunity to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend the Cheese Club :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Yosemite it is stunning!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit difficult in the beginning to adjust the the large population of homeless compared to Denmark. It can also be quite difficult to make friends during lectures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet other exchange students. Join clubs and societies that is how local students socialize, only few Berkeley students socialize during lecture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Americans are very kind and easy to talk to. It is not unusual that someone will come up to you and compliments your outfit :). 
Berkeley students (within the Bioengineering department at least) are highly motivated and get shit done. Every time I had to do a group presentation, every single person in the group was very dedicated and finished stuff on time. I really appreciated that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Take a fun course like a dcal course
- Ask for help from fellow exchange students!
- join a club or sports team etc.!
- Remember that maybe it can be lonely in the beginning but you will make friends.
- start scholarship (legat) applications early

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not as difficult to pass courses compared to Copenhagen University.. so remember to enjoy your time in the US. Furthermore remember that your grade is actually up for debate. You can contact the professor and ask them what you can do to get a better grade (which I am really not used to). So if you are about to pass a course, go talk to the professor.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in the US and the friends that I made <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: making friends while also balancing school. It was difficult for me to go out and socialize when I have had a full day of school and assignments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
